ledger_rows: | EN-1 | **How `0026EE00`'s two integer arguments combine.** | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 — they MULTIPLY.** With the row zero, either argument alone gives `0` and the pair gives `min(255, (a·b) >> 7)`. The full rule is **`out = min(255, (2·((row·(a+b)) mod 256) + ((a·b) >> 7)) mod 512)`** — **1,331 of 1,331** exhaustive combinations, plus **120 of 120** hold-out on each of byte positions 0, 2 and 3. The old single-argument formula is its **`b = 0` case**, reproduced exactly. The six deviations of `+1`, `+2` and once `+12` are the cross term `(a·b) >> 7`; the last piece was the **nine-bit intermediate** — four placements of the saturation all plateaued at 1,256 of 1,331 and every failure was the sum **mod 512**. Apparatus kept as `workbench_probe.py`. [the workbench has a save and a restore](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Shared-Transform-Workbench/the-workbench-has-a-save-and-restore-and-nine-functions-use-it.md) §6. |

ledger_rows: | I-6 | ~~Where the dispatch index mapping breaks.~~ | **CLOSED 2026-09-07 — there is no discontinuity, and this is now exhaustive rather than sampled.** `record N = verb N` holds across all **1,496** family-0 records. **645 independent anchors** — verbs the ff12-script catalog knows, each with an argument count, against the VM operand count measured from the handler body, two numbers neither derived from the other — agree at **89.1 %**, spanning `0x0000`-`0x05D7` at a mean spacing of **2.32 records**. **The counterfactual is what makes it a proof:** shift the table one record and the same comparison gives **55.7 %**. **Re-run 2026-09-07 with a second, oppositely-biased metric** (`net = pops − pushes`): **612 anchors, 97.2 % against a 59.0 % shifted baseline.** Two instruments that are wrong in opposite directions both place the identity mapping 33-38 points above its own shifted baseline. Agreement per 128-record bucket ranges 77.6-100 % with **no step anywhere**, and a slip at record K would give ~56 % above K. The disagreements are a **catalog gap, not a mapping gap** — and under `net` there are only **17**. ⚠ **The explanation first published for them is RETRACTED:** it read the `+1` cluster as *"popping the handle of the thing being waited on"*. **The bodies say otherwise** — the shared `begin` `0x0034C290` pushes a literal `0` and pops it straight back, so the handler supplies its own operand and the catalog's zero was correct. The over-generalisation *"every one durative"* is also wrong: seven of those fifteen verbs are instantaneous. **Residual, stated rather than rounded away:** a compensating pair of shifts falling entirely inside one anchor-free window is not excluded; **the largest such window is 25 records.** No single shift of any size survives. **The 2026-09-02 withdrawal got the right answer by a circular route** and is corrected in `COVERAGE.md`. |

ledger_rows: | EE-3 | ~~**What distinguishes the two completion arms**, and what sets bit 0 of battle-unit `+0xE99` that chooses between them.~~ **ANSWERED 2026-09-10 (FABLE).** The verb's **mode** argument: `00239710` writes `+0xE99` bit 0 = `(mode == 1)` and bit 1 = `(mode == 2)` (`0023974D`–`00239766`). Mode 1 raises the ledger flag in the same call and dispatches `0x2005`, which the reaction handler routes to `BattleUnit_TryCommitEngageAutoAttack` (`0032515E`); any other mode dispatches the death reaction `0x2008` and sets unit bit 47, and the flag is raised by `00307110` when the reaction handler processes `0x2007/0x2008/0x200C/0x200E` (jump-table case `00325185`, `0032519C`→`003251A4`). **Both arms converge on ledger `flags` bit 0**, consumed once per field frame by `00307030` into `u16` slot 3 of the table at `*(02098E68)`. Bit 1 (mode 2) is read by `BattleUnit_TeardownAndDespawn` at `00300F89` — `EE-10`. **Caveat, same day:** `00307110`'s only caller `003250F0` is reached by **no static route of any enumerated form** (system page §5, `EE-12`), so as read the deferred arm sets bit 47, plays `0x2008` and never posts; only mode-1 groups reach slot 3. It writes records **2, 3, 4** at `01DF1738`, never 0 and 1, and sets `mgr[+0x3B]` — the dirty flag `00196FF0` consumes. **Group 2's four slots are never published** (the read span covers 24 of 28 dwords).
